Loading performance, browser rendering, perceived performance, resource optimization, Core Web Vitals (CWV), caching strategies, and the technical mechanics of shrinking file sizes and reducing execution time. Specifically capturing the definitions and optimization tactics for Largest Contentful Paint (LCP), First Input Delay (FID), and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS).

why: Provides baseline definitions for Core Web Vitals (LCP, FID, CLS) and explains mechanical optimization tactics like setting image aspect ratios, utilizing preload links, and analyzing performance across an entire domain using Unlighthouse.

core web vitals / Understanding the three primary metrics of Google's Core Web Vitals. Largest Contentful Paint (LCP): measures loading performance, tracking the time it takes to render the largest image or text block. LCP must occur within 2.5 seconds (anything over 4 seconds negatively impacts SEO). Optimizations include compressing images (using WebP formats), utilizing CDNs (like Firebase or Vercel), minimizing render-blocking JavaScript, and using HTML preload links and fetchpriority attributes on critical assets. First Input Delay (FID): measures interactivity, tracking the time from a user's first click to the browser's response. FID must be under 100 milliseconds. Optimizations include reducing JavaScript execution time via lazy loading, using frameworks like Qwik, or offloading scripts to Web Workers (via tools like Partytown). Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS): measures visual stability, tracking unexpected page jumps. Optimizations include explicitly defining image dimensions (width and height) or using the CSS aspect-ratio property, and utilizing the srcset attribute for responsive images to reserve space before they load.

auditing tools / Using the Chrome Network Tab waterfall to identify asset bottlenecks. Installing the Web Vitals Chrome Extension to log specific DOM elements causing LCP or CLS issues directly in the browser console. Running Unlighthouse (npx unlighthouse --site <url>) to perform parallel Lighthouse audits across hundreds of URLs simultaneously to find outlier pages with poor performance.

Look for. The specific LCP threshold: good is <2.5 seconds, poor is >4.0 seconds. The specific FID threshold: good is <100 milliseconds, poor is >300 milliseconds. The CSS attribute used to prevent CLS without hardcoding exact pixels: aspect-ratio. The tool to offload third-party scripts to a Web Worker: Partytown. The exact terminal command to run site-wide audits: npx unlighthouse.
Skip. Plugs for Fireship Pro. The subjective analysis of Amazon, Reddit, or Astro's homepage scores.
